PainterlyNPR__MaterialAssignment__Config.ConfigNote: How a material class given to an object or a face is carried through the drawing: which classes lay courses, what a face is, and the sample each class is drawn on for its swatch.

PainterlyNPR__MaterialAssignment__Config.Note: Where the Materials tab reads the material library, and where the factory writes its swatches
PainterlyNPR__MaterialAssignment__Config.RootNote: From the engine's root (the folder holding 02__Src__AppModules), resolved from the engine's own files rather than the page (v0.8.2): a wrapper that pins the engine pins the register and swatches beside it in the same layout
PainterlyNPR__MaterialAssignment__Config.ApiNote: The local server's: POST /api/materials/<Key>/<RND|PXY> writes a swatch into the class's group folder
PainterlyNPR__MaterialAssignment__Config.MaxAssignmentsNote: A drawing holds this many material assignments at most; giving a class again to what already has one replaces it rather than adding

PainterlyNPR__MaterialAssignment__Config.Note: A material is a class (13__Scene__MaterialClasses): its wash, its albedo, its hatching - and, for a few, the courses material indication lays. Giving a class to an object or a face carries all of it: the wash and hatching follow at once (they read each pixel's class), and the courses follow by Patterns.
PainterlyNPR__MaterialAssignment__Config.ExcludedNote: The sky is not a surface: nothing is given it
PainterlyNPR__MaterialAssignment__Config.PatternsNote: The classes that lay courses, and which. A surface given any other class keeps no courses; a face given one of these gets courses even if it had none
PainterlyNPR__MaterialAssignment__Config.LaidNote: A pattern laid after every assignment on each flat face whose triangles end up in its class, however they came by it (a whole object or a face given it, a SketchUp swatch, a rule, a host's scene file), within what the face and its linework leave clear (FaceMask). A project's own model (GLB) carries no surfaces, so it lays all of these: Adam, 03-Nov-2026, 'Sketchup dosnt render the brickwork either, ensure all material linework is added'. Everywhere: stone is also laid on a demo scene's walls, whose brick and tile come from the builders. Slope: what a face must be (Upright a wall, Pitched anything a tile can lie on, Level a floor). MinAreaM2, MinHeightM: the smallest face that counts, so a brick plinth takes courses and a fascia no stones. MaskMinM2, MaskMinShare: a clear patch counts when it is at least this big and this share of the face's biggest, so a window's pane, closed off by its own lines, takes nothing. MaskCloseCells: how far a line shuts the cells round it, 1 keeping stones off every line, 0 letting courses run right up to one. OutlineCloses: whether the face's own outline counts as such a line. Courses run to their face's edge; stones keep off it
PainterlyNPR__MaterialAssignment__Config.LayMaxTrianglesNote: An object heavier than this lays no courses (a Slope needs its faces walked, and a mesh this fine is not brickwork): stone, which is asked for, is still laid
PainterlyNPR__MaterialAssignment__Config.SoldierNeedsNote: A soldier course over an opening stays only while its wall is brick
PainterlyNPR__MaterialAssignment__Config.FlagNeedsNote: A flagstone path keeps its flags only while it is paving

PainterlyNPR__MaterialAssignment__Config.Note: A face is what SketchUp would call one: the triangles of one object that lie in one plane and join edge to edge, found from the one picked. A plant's masses are smooth, so a face on a plant is the plant.
PainterlyNPR__MaterialAssignment__Config.NormalDotNote: Two triangles face the same way when their normals agree this well (about 2.5 degrees)
PainterlyNPR__MaterialAssignment__Config.PlaneMNote: And lie in one plane within this many metres
PainterlyNPR__MaterialAssignment__Config.WeldMNote: Corners nearer than this are one corner when edges are matched
PainterlyNPR__MaterialAssignment__Config.OffsetMNote: A new face's courses sit this far proud of it, as every surface's do
PainterlyNPR__MaterialAssignment__Config.UprightNyNote: A face counts as a wall when its normal rises no more than this
PainterlyNPR__MaterialAssignment__Config.LevelNyNote: And as a floor when it rises at least this much; between them it is a pitch. Either way up: a SketchUp face is often modelled back to front, and the truth buffer says what shows
PainterlyNPR__MaterialAssignment__Config.MaskCellMNote: What is clear on a face, measured in cells this size. A whitecard's wall is often one flat rectangle with its windows and quoins only drawn on it, so the face alone cannot say where a stone may go: its linework must
PainterlyNPR__MaterialAssignment__Config.MaskReachMNote: A line of any object this near the face's plane, both ends, keeps a material's marks off it: quoins and window surrounds stand a little proud, and a wall painted in SketchUp is a bucket of its own, its lines on another object
PainterlyNPR__MaterialAssignment__Config.MaskWallM2Note: A patch this big is open wall whatever the share: no pane is, and the biggest patch of a wall may be behind a new building (Thrower's existing rear wall, painted Stonework, kept its stones out of sight and none where it shows)

PainterlyNPR__MaterialAssignment__Config.Note: What each class is drawn on for its swatch in the catalogue environment: a block for what buildings are made of, a slab for what the ground is made of, a mound for planting, a log for bark.
PainterlyNPR__MaterialAssignment__Config.BlockMNote: Width, height and depth of the block: a stretch of wall's worth, its courses at true gauge
PainterlyNPR__MaterialAssignment__Config.LogMNote: The log's radius and height: a short upright trunk
